_doc: R41: veterancy and the Sparring Ring. A chimera earns xp from every battle it walks out of — win or lose, because showing up against something real teaches something real — sized by the opposition's scale and wave count, and its LEVEL multiplies hp, power, armor and stamina (never speed: how fast a creature acts is anatomy — mass, lift, physiology — and veterancy must not scramble the turn order the body earned). Grades are what a chimera IS BUILT from; levels are what it has BEEN THROUGH. The design brief, verbatim from the player: 'a chimera you create at the beginning of the game should be able to last the entire game.' statPerLevel is tuned against the measured finale, not stat parity: grade also sharpens MOVES (+12% per grade), so equal stats are not an equal fight. At 0.05 (L10 = +50%), a day-one Standard wings team at max level takes The Boardroom at 63% — better than a fresh Apex L0 team of the same build (44%) — while kite and noise stay at 0% there, so levels reward the right matchup rather than replacing it; 0.06 was measured and rejected because it washed matchups out (94%). Mid-game, the walls open at a few levels: Precinct for a Ground team goes 0% at L0 to 34% at L3 and 50% at L5. levels[] are cumulative xp thresholds: level = how many entries xp has reached; maxLevel is levels.length. Sparring: a procedural rematch drawn from a node you already HOLD, at sparScale of that encounter's tier, for sparringFraction of the xp — no purse, no notoriety, no capture on a loss (nobody impounds a sparring partner), but real injuries, because a training accident is still an accident. sparCooldownHours is a real-world timestamp cooldown (house rule: timers are timestamps), long enough that real assaults stay the better xp per evening, short enough that a walled player can climb out. Adding xp values or levels here must never require engine edits.
sparBlurbs: The tarps are down, the crash mats are out, and the garrison has agreed to pretend this is a drill.
A rematch, for science. The loser buys the antiseptic.
Full contact, no paperwork. The best kind of continuing education.
The opposition sent their B-squad. Your creatures could use the cardio.
Somebody chalked a ring on the tarmac. Attendance is mandatory, dignity optional.
